content.title: India's IT shares near three‑year low as OpenAI move revives AI fears
content.summary: India's IT shares fell to a three-year low on Tuesday as investor jitters around the threat posed by artificial intelligence to flagship IT firms flared ‌up again, after OpenAI announced a new AI venture.  The Nifty IT index fell 3.6% to ‌its lowest since May 2023, with Tata Consultancy Services, Infosys, HCL Technologies and Wipro falling between 2.5% and 4%.  Analysts at HSBC ​said in a Tuesday note that India's top-tier IT firms largely failed to meet street expectations for earnings in March quarter as well as in their outlooks for the new financial year, adding that strong spending globally on AI could be "crowding out" demand for traditional IT services.

business_news.title: Ariana Resources, Amigo Resources, Future PLC, ACG Metals, Quantum Blockchain Technologies
business_news.summary: Ariana Resources PLC (AIM:AAU, ASX:AA2, FRA:4A6) has confirmed that gold mineralisation at its Dokwe project in Zimbabwe extends at least 150 metres beyond the current resource envelope, with all assays now received from the latest drilling campaign. A JORC resource update is planned for the second half of 2026. Amigo Resources PLC (LSE:AMGO, FRA:0VG) has secured two processing licences in Tanzania, giving it the regulatory green light to advance modular mineral processing hubs at Kabete Mines and Mojimoto. The next phase includes metallurgical test work, drilling and progressive integration of artisanal feedstock into a centralised processing model. Future PLC (LSE:FUTR) has held its full-year guidance despite an 8% drop in first-half revenue, pointing to improving trends across all three divisions in the second quarter. The specialist media group still expects a mid to low single-digit organic revenue decline for the full year with EBITDA margins of 25% to 27%. ACG Metals Ltd (LSE:ACG, OTC:ACGAF) has made its shares eligible for electronic clearing through the Depository Trust Company in the US, making it easier for American investors to access and trade the stock. The shares will continue to settle through CREST in the UK as well. Quantum Blockchain Technologies PLC (AIM:QBT, FRA:BYA1) has extended the maturity of its remaining €2.873 million zero-coupon bond by two years to December 2028.
